codes.meaning: The check you named is not something this run is warning about. An answer is only meaningful against something the tool is currently saying.
codes.name: NOT_WARNED
codes.remedy: Answer one of the warnings this run raised — the message lists them. If it raised none, run the checks first.
codes.summary: Raised when an answer names something nothing is warning about.

codes.meaning: That password is too short to be the one. It is the only thing standing in front of a surface that can start, stop and reconfigure everything, and what is on the other side of it is a program that guesses without getting bored.
codes.name: TOO_SHORT
codes.remedy: Use at least twelve characters. Several unrelated words are easier to keep and harder to guess than one word with substitutions in it.
codes.summary: Raised when a password is too short to stand in front of this.

codes.meaning: The password could not be recorded. Every stored password is mixed with unpredictable bytes so that two of them are never written down the same way, and this machine would not supply any.
codes.name: NO_SALT
codes.remedy: Try again. If it happens twice, the operating system's own random source is at fault.
codes.summary: Raised when this machine will not supply the salt a record is made with.

codes.meaning: The two passwords typed were not the same, and nothing was changed. It is asked for twice because nothing here can read one back afterwards, so the second answer is the only check there is that the first was typed the way it was meant.
codes.name: MISTYPED
codes.remedy: Set it again, typing the same password both times.
codes.summary: Raised when the two answers were not the same word.

codes.meaning: The request carried no token or session this run admits, and nothing was answered. The sentence does not say which it was: it answers somebody who has proved nothing, and naming what was wrong would tell them what to keep guessing at.
codes.name: NOT_ADMITTED
codes.remedy: Sign in again, or open lemonfiber from the address it printed when it started.
codes.summary: Raised when a request carried no token, session or key this run admits.

codes.meaning: The request said it came from somewhere this server is not. The address it named, or the page it came from, is not the one this server is listening on, and nothing was answered.
codes.name: ELSEWHERE
codes.remedy: Reach lemonfiber at the address it is listening on.
codes.summary: Raised when a request said it came from somewhere this server is not.

codes.meaning: This is not something this account may ask for. Nothing is wrong with the account: what was asked for belongs to somebody else, or to whoever looks after this machine.
codes.name: NOT_YOURS
codes.remedy: Ask whoever looks after this machine, if you need it.
codes.summary: Raised when an account asked for something that is not its to ask for.

codes.meaning: The account could not be checked with the media server, so nobody was identified and nothing was answered. The account has not been removed, the session has not ended, and nothing about the account changed.
codes.name: UNCONFIRMED
codes.remedy: Try again once the media server is running.
codes.summary: Raised when the media server could not say whether an account is still one.

codes.meaning: That is not the password for this machine. Nothing was opened, and no session was begun. The same is said where no password is set, so whoever is knocking cannot tell whether there is anything here to guess at.
codes.name: NOT_THE_PASSWORD
codes.remedy: Check the password and try again.
codes.summary: Raised when the password offered at the door was wrong, or none is set.

codes.meaning: Too many wrong passwords. The door has stopped looking at passwords for a while, and another attempt now makes the wait longer. The message says how long, and so does the answer's `Retry-After` header.
codes.name: TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS
codes.remedy: Wait as long as it says, then try once more.
codes.summary: Raised when the door has been given too many wrong passwords lately.

codes.meaning: What was offered at the door is not a password. The door reads a password, and a household member's name beside it, and the body carried neither in a form it can read.
codes.name: NOT_A_PASSWORD
codes.remedy: Send the password as the body's `password`.
codes.summary: Raised when what was offered at the door is not a password.

codes.meaning: A key, or a request to mint one, arrived from another machine over a connection its pin does not verify, and nothing was answered or minted. A key or a secret crosses a network only over the encrypted connection whose certificate the key was minted with, because one sent any other way may have been read on the way.
codes.name: KEY_IN_THE_CLEAR
codes.remedy: Connect over https, pinning the certificate the key was minted with, and revoke the key with `lemonfiber key revoke` if it may have been read.
codes.summary: Raised when a key arrived from another machine over a connection its pin does not verify.

codes.meaning: The key asked for something its scope does not reach, and nothing was done. A key has one scope — `read`, `act` or one member's own — and admits that and nothing more.
codes.name: NOT_FOR_A_KEY
codes.remedy: Call only what the contract lists as callable by a key, or ask whoever looks after this machine.
codes.summary: Raised when a key asked for something its scope does not reach.

codes.meaning: There is no action by that name. An action here is a command the command line offers, and this surface offers nothing else. The message names what was asked for.
codes.name: NO_SUCH_ACTION
codes.remedy: Ask for one of the actions the contract names.
codes.summary: Raised where no action goes by the name that was asked for.

codes.meaning: An action was not given an argument it needs, so it was not carried out. The message names the action and the argument.
codes.name: MISSING_ARGUMENT
codes.remedy: Ask again with the arguments the action takes.
codes.summary: Raised where an action was not given an argument it needs.

codes.meaning: An argument was given a value that names nothing this stack knows. The message names the argument, what it said, and what it could have said instead.
codes.name: UNRECOGNISED_ARGUMENT
codes.remedy: Ask again with the arguments the action takes.
codes.summary: Raised where an argument was given a value that names nothing.

codes.meaning: An action was given an argument its command has nowhere to put. It is refused rather than dropped, because dropping it would carry out a different request from the one asked for.
codes.name: UNWANTED_ARGUMENT
codes.remedy: Ask again with the arguments the action takes.
codes.summary: Raised where an action was given an argument its command has nowhere to put.

codes.meaning: An action was given two arguments that each name a different request. A run carrying both would have to pick one of them and answer something nobody asked for. The message names the two.
codes.name: ARGUMENTS_TOGETHER
codes.remedy: Ask again with the arguments the action takes, choosing one of the two.
codes.summary: Raised where two arguments that each name a different request arrived together.

codes.meaning: The body of the request is not arguments the action can read. What the reader could not take from it — a field it did not know, or where the text stopped being JSON — is given as the detail.
codes.name: NOT_ARGUMENTS
codes.remedy: Ask again with the arguments the action takes.
codes.summary: Raised where the body of an action is not arguments it can read.

codes.meaning: No work in this run goes by that name. Jobs are named by the run that starts them, and work from an earlier run is not tracked here.
codes.name: NO_SUCH_JOB
codes.remedy: Ask about a job this run started.
codes.summary: Raised where a job was asked about that this run did not start.

codes.meaning: The body of a setup step is not one of setup's answers, nor a way out of an interrupted apply, so setup did not move. What arrived is not repeated back, because an answer can carry a credential.
codes.name: NOT_AN_ANSWER
codes.remedy: Answer the question setup is asking.
codes.summary: Raised where the body of a setup step is not an answer it can read.

codes.meaning: No endpoint answers this path. Every endpoint this surface answers is named in the contract, and this path is not one of them.
codes.name: NO_ENDPOINT
codes.remedy: Ask for one of the endpoints the contract names.
codes.summary: Raised where a path under the endpoints is one no endpoint answers.

codes.meaning: The path is one this surface answers, asked with a method it does not answer it with, and nothing was done.
codes.name: WRONG_METHOD
codes.remedy: Ask again with the method the contract names.
codes.summary: Raised where an endpoint was asked with a method it does not answer.

codes.meaning: The body of a request to mint a key is not a key's name, scope and purpose with the password, so no key was minted.
codes.name: NOT_A_KEY_REQUEST
codes.remedy: Send the name, scope, purpose and password as the body's four fields.
codes.summary: Raised where the body of a mint is not a key's name, scope, purpose and the password.

codes.meaning: An action's `Idempotency-Key` is not one to 255 visible characters, or was given more than once. The action was not carried out, and nothing was changed: a key that cannot be read is one a second send could not be recognised by.
codes.name: NOT_AN_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY
codes.remedy: Send the key once, as up to 255 visible characters with no spaces.
codes.summary: Raised where an action's `Idempotency-Key` is not one to 255 visible characters, or is given more than once.

codes.meaning: This `Idempotency-Key` was already sent with another action or other arguments. Nothing was carried out under it a second time; the attempt it names asked for something else, and that is what it was answered with.
codes.name: IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED
codes.remedy: Send a new key with each new attempt, and the same key only with the same action sent again.
codes.summary: Raised where an `Idempotency-Key` already sent with one action and its arguments is sent with another.

codes.meaning: There is not enough room. A backup is written to the same disk it protects, and this one would not fit with room to spare. Nothing was captured.
codes.name: NO_ROOM
codes.remedy: Free space on the backups volume, or lower how many backups are kept.
codes.summary: Raised when there is not enough room to write a backup.

codes.meaning: The archive could not be written and the capture stopped part-way. A configuration backup is what makes the rest recoverable, so it is worth fixing before a risky change.
codes.name: NOT_WRITTEN
codes.remedy: Check the backups volume is writable, then try again.
codes.summary: Raised when the backup archive could not be written.

codes.meaning: The room for a backup could not be measured. lemonfiber checks a backup will fit before starting one. Nothing was captured.
codes.name: NOT_MEASURED
codes.remedy: Check the backups location is reachable, then try again.
codes.summary: Raised when the room for a backup could not be measured.

codes.meaning: The stack was not confirmed stopped, so nothing was captured. Copying a database a service is writing to is the corruption a backup exists to prevent, so a running stack — and an engine that will not say whether it is running — are refused alike.
codes.name: STILL_RUNNING
codes.remedy: Stop the stack, check the container engine is answering, then capture again.
codes.summary: Raised when a capture could not be shown that nothing is writing to a database.

codes.meaning: This run has nowhere it knows to keep an archive. A backup goes into lemonfiber's own directory, and this machine would not say where that is. Nothing was written.
codes.name: NOWHERE_TO_KEEP
codes.remedy: Set a home directory for this user, then capture again.
codes.summary: Raised when this run has nowhere it knows to keep an archive.

codes.meaning: This run has nowhere it knows to look for backups. They are kept in lemonfiber's own directory, and this machine would not say where that is, so there is nowhere to read a list of them from.
codes.name: NOWHERE_KEPT
codes.remedy: Set a home directory for this user, then ask again.
codes.summary: Raised when this run has nowhere it knows to look for archives.

codes.meaning: The backups kept here could not be listed. The directory lemonfiber keeps them in would not be read, so what is in it is not known. Nothing was touched.
codes.name: NOT_LISTED
codes.remedy: Check the backups directory is readable, then ask again.
codes.summary: Raised when the directory the archives are kept in could not be read.

codes.meaning: A service the stack calls an admin service is reachable from your network. It is meant to answer this machine and nothing else: it can change how your stack works, and most services like it have weak or no password of their own, so anything on your network reaching it is a way in.
codes.name: BEYOND_LOOPBACK
codes.remedy: Publish it on this machine only, and apply the change. The message names the address to use. Or, if you meant to expose it, say so once and say why, with `LEMONFIBER_EXPOSED=<service>=<why>` in your settings.
codes.summary: Raised when a service the stack calls admin answers somewhere off this machine.

codes.meaning: A firewall rule on this machine may not apply to the ports the stack publishes. The container engine runs directly on this machine here, and it writes its own forwarding rules ahead of the ones you add, so a port you believe is shut may still answer. This is how publishing is meant to work and nothing is broken.
codes.name: AROUND_THE_FIREWALL
codes.remedy: Narrow what the household tier is published on, which is what does decide: `LAN_BIND` in your settings, set to this machine's own address on your network. Or leave it, if every device on this network is one you would let in anyway.
codes.summary: Raised where a published port is reached without the host's own firewall rules being consulted.

codes.meaning: An admin service is reachable from your network and you have written down that you meant it to. It is still reported, because the exposure is real either way; what changed is whose decision it is. The message quotes your reason back.
codes.name: DELIBERATE
codes.remedy: Nothing, if that is still true. Or take it out of the exposed list and publish it on this machine only.
codes.summary: Raised where an admin service answers off this machine and the operator has written down that they meant it to.

codes.meaning: The finished bundle still held something that reads as a credential, so nothing was written. A bundle is a thing people post in public, so anything in one that still looks like a key is treated as one — even where it turns out not to be.
codes.name: BUNDLE_LEAK
codes.remedy: Report which file the message names, so the value it holds can be added to what a bundle knows how to replace.
codes.summary: Raised when a bundle would still hold something that reads as a credential.

codes.meaning: There is not enough room to write the bundle where it was to be written, with space left over for the machine to keep working in.
codes.name: BUNDLE_NO_ROOM
codes.remedy: Free some space, or write the bundle somewhere with more room using `--out`.
codes.summary: Raised when there is not enough room to write a bundle.

codes.meaning: The archive could not be written. Nothing was left behind: a bundle is written whole or not at all, so there is no half-file to mistake for one.
codes.name: BUNDLE_UNWRITTEN
codes.remedy: Check the path is writable, then ask for the bundle again.
codes.summary: Raised when the archive could not be written.

codes.meaning: A setting was asked to be shown as it is, without that being confirmed on the same run. Showing one puts the real value in a file people post in public, so it takes saying twice.
codes.name: BUNDLE_UNCONFIRMED
codes.remedy: Run it again with `--confirm` if you meant it.
codes.summary: Raised when a setting was asked to be shown as it is without that being confirmed.

codes.meaning: The machine could offer no randomness to derive the stand-ins from, so nothing was written. A stand-in anyone can reproduce is a way back to the value it stands for.
codes.name: BUNDLE_NO_MARKS
codes.remedy: Report this. A machine that cannot produce random bytes is a fault in its own right.
codes.summary: Raised when the machine can offer no randomness to derive stand-ins from.

codes.meaning: This run can write no archive at all: it holds neither a directory of its own to keep one in nor anything to pack one with, which is what a machine that will not say where its own files go leaves behind. A bundle asked for at a named path is refused here too, and nothing was written.
codes.name: NOWHERE_TO_KEEP
codes.remedy: Set a home directory for this user, then ask for the bundle again.
codes.summary: Raised when this run has nowhere it knows to keep a bundle.

codes.meaning: This run has nowhere it knows to look for a bundle. Bundles asked for by name are kept with lemonfiber's own files, and this machine would not say where those are, so there is nowhere to read one back from.
codes.name: NOWHERE_HELD
codes.remedy: Set a home directory for this user, then ask for the bundle again.
codes.summary: Raised when this run has nowhere it knows to look for a bundle it kept.

codes.meaning: The name you gave is not one of the bundles kept here. A bundle asked for by name is one of the files this run wrote into lemonfiber's own directory; a name holding a path, or climbing out of that directory, is refused rather than followed.
codes.name: NOT_HELD
codes.remedy: Ask for a bundle by the name the run that produced it reported.
codes.summary: Raised when a name does not name one of the bundles this run kept.

codes.meaning: Your settings exist and could not be read. Nothing has been changed — lemonfiber will not guess at settings it cannot read.
codes.name: CONFIG_UNREADABLE
codes.remedy: Check the file is readable. The message names its path.
codes.summary: Raised when configuration exists and cannot be read.

codes.meaning: Your settings could not be saved. The change was not made and your existing settings are untouched.
codes.name: CONFIG_NOT_WRITTEN
codes.remedy: Check the location is writable and has space.
codes.summary: Raised when configuration cannot be written.

codes.meaning: There is nowhere to keep settings, because setup has not chosen a location yet.
codes.name: CONFIG_NOWHERE
codes.remedy: Run `lemonfiber setup`.
codes.summary: Raised when there is nowhere to keep configuration.

codes.meaning: A file holding a credential can be read by somebody other than its owner. Nothing has been changed — this is the doctor reporting what it found.
codes.name: CREDENTIALS_EXPOSED
codes.remedy: Take the permissions back to their owner. The message names each file.
codes.summary: Raised when a file holding a credential can be read by more than its owner.

codes.meaning: Your settings were written by a newer lemonfiber than the one running, so this build will not write over them. Nothing has been changed — an older build writing over a newer one's settings leaves a file neither version can make sense of, and no way back to the one you had.
codes.name: CONFIG_TOO_NEW
codes.remedy: Run the newer lemonfiber, or take this one forward with `lemonfiber update self`. The message names both versions.
codes.summary: Raised when configuration was written by a newer lemonfiber.

codes.meaning: A value could not be saved because it has a line break in it. Nothing has been changed — the settings file holds one setting per line, so the rest of the value would have been read as settings you never chose.
codes.name: CONFIG_SPANS_LINES
codes.remedy: Check where the value came from, and set it to a single line. The message names the settings file.
codes.summary: Raised when a setting's key or value spans more than one line.

codes.meaning: The Usenet indexer aggregator answers its whole configuration — the indexer accounts it holds, and their keys among it — to anything that can reach it, or could not be asked whether it does. Nothing has been changed — this is the doctor reporting what it found.
codes.name: AGGREGATOR_EXPOSED
codes.remedy: Run `lemonfiber seed` to turn its authentication on, or `lemonfiber reset` where you turned it off yourself. Where it could not be asked, check it is up and has finished starting, then run the diagnosis again.
codes.summary: Raised when the Usenet indexer aggregator answers a read of its whole configuration to a caller presenting nothing, or will not say whether it does.

codes.meaning: A service answered and refused the credential it generated itself. The key in its configuration no longer matches the one the running service expects, usually because the configuration was regenerated after the service last started.
codes.name: CREDENTIAL_REJECTED
codes.remedy: Restart the service so it reloads its configuration, then check again: `lemonfiber restart`.
codes.summary: Raised when a service answers and refuses the credential it generated itself.

codes.meaning: The indexer answered and rejected the API key configured for it. The key is wrong, expired, or for a different indexer — searches through it come back empty.
codes.name: INDEXER_REJECTED
codes.remedy: Correct the indexer's API key in configuration, then check again.
codes.summary: Raised when the indexer answers and refuses the key it was given.

codes.meaning: The indexer accepted the key and would not serve the request — usually a rate or quota limit that lifts on its own. The key is not wrong.
codes.name: INDEXER_LIMITED
codes.remedy: Leave it a while and check again.
codes.summary: Raised when the indexer authenticates the key but cannot serve it right now.

codes.meaning: The decline service's key was used later than anything the service recorded doing with it. That is either the service doing something it should not, or the key in somebody else's hands. The message gives when it was used, and when the service last recorded something, if it ever did.
codes.name: UNEXPLAINED
codes.remedy: If nobody declined an invitation or had one run out then, rotate the key with `lemonfiber credentials rotate`, and check what the decline service is running.
codes.summary: Raised when the decline service's key was used later than anything the service recorded doing with it.

codes.meaning: Nothing on this stack reports under the name you narrowed the run to. A check is named by the identifier its finding carries, and no finding here carries that one. Answering with an empty report would read as nothing being wrong.
codes.name: NO_SUCH_CHECK
codes.remedy: Run the checks with `lemonfiber doctor`, and narrow to a name this stack reports.
codes.summary: Raised when a run is narrowed to a check nothing in this stack reports.

codes.meaning: The container engine is not running. Nothing about your stack can be read or changed while it is down.
codes.name: ENGINE_UNREACHABLE
codes.remedy: Start Docker Desktop, or the `docker` service on Linux. This is the first thing to fix.
codes.summary: Raised when the container engine cannot be reached.

codes.meaning: A container that should be up is not. It may have stopped on its own, or never been started.
codes.name: NO_SUCH_CONTAINER
codes.remedy: Start the form that includes it. `lemonfiber ps` shows what is running.
codes.summary: Raised when a container that should exist does not.

codes.meaning: The host an endpoint names could not be found on the network. The name was looked up and nothing answered to it, so no connection was attempted — the daemon may be running perfectly on a machine this one cannot name.
codes.name: HOST_UNRESOLVED
codes.remedy: Check the host name, and that this machine can resolve it. Trying the host's address in place of its name tells the two apart.
codes.summary: Raised when the host an endpoint names cannot be found on the network.

codes.meaning: The host was found and refused the connection. The name is right and something about the endpoint is not: either Docker is not running over there, or it is not listening where the endpoint says.
codes.name: HOST_REFUSED
codes.remedy: Check Docker is running on that machine, and on the port the endpoint names.
codes.summary: Raised when the host is found and refuses the connection.

codes.meaning: The host was reached and would not accept the SSH login. This is about keys and accounts rather than about Docker — lemonfiber uses the SSH configuration you already have and makes no keys of its own.
codes.name: LOGIN_REJECTED
codes.remedy: Connect to the host with `ssh` and read what it says, then try again.
codes.summary: Raised when the host is reached and will not accept the SSH login.

codes.meaning: The endpoint names a transport lemonfiber cannot drive. Nothing was read and nothing was changed, because reading one machine while writing to another is worse than reaching neither.
codes.name: ENDPOINT_UNSUPPORTED
codes.remedy: Point `DOCKER_HOST` at an `ssh://` or `tcp://` endpoint, or at a local socket.
codes.summary: Raised when an endpoint names a transport this build cannot drive.

codes.meaning: A Docker context was named and this machine records no endpoint under that name. Nothing was read and nothing was changed, because falling back to the local daemon would answer about this machine while you were asking about another.
codes.name: UNKNOWN_CONTEXT
codes.remedy: List the contexts this machine has with `docker context ls`, and name one of those.
codes.summary: Raised when a named Docker context is not one this machine records.

codes.meaning: A remote host did not answer, for a reason nothing here recognises. What the transport said is quoted beside it; it names that machine rather than this one.
codes.name: HOST_SILENT
codes.remedy: Read what the transport said. It is the most specific thing known about this.
codes.summary: Raised when a remote host does not answer for a reason nothing here recognises.

codes.meaning: Docker is not installed. lemonfiber runs your stack in containers, so nothing can start without an engine.
codes.name: DOCKER_ABSENT
codes.remedy: Install Docker Desktop, or Docker Engine on Linux.
codes.summary: Raised when the Docker client is not installed.

codes.meaning: Docker is installed and its daemon is not answering, or would not start. The client being present usually means this is the daemon stopped, or a permission problem, rather than a missing install.
codes.name: DAEMON_DOWN
codes.remedy: Start Docker Desktop, or the `docker` service on Linux. If it is running, check that your account may run `docker`.
codes.summary: Raised when the Docker client is present but its daemon is not answering.

codes.meaning: The Docker Compose plugin is missing, or is too old. lemonfiber drives the stack through Compose v2.
codes.name: COMPOSE_UNUSABLE
codes.remedy: Install or update the Docker Compose plugin. The message names the minimum version.
codes.summary: Raised when the Compose plugin is missing or too old to drive.

codes.meaning: The container engine is not set to start with this machine. The containers carry a restart policy, and a restart policy only brings a container back once the engine behind it is running — so after the next restart the stack is simply not there, with no error and nothing in any log you would think to look at.
codes.name: ENGINE_NOT_AT_BOOT
codes.remedy: Turn the engine's own start-at-boot on: Docker Desktop's open-at-login setting on a Mac and on Windows, the daemon's unit on Linux. The message names which.
codes.summary: Raised when the container engine is confirmed not to start with this machine. One code for both arrangements it can be. What is not set differs by platform — Docker Desktop's open-at-login setting on macOS and Windows, the daemon's own unit on native Linux — and what has gone wrong is the same thing either way: nothing brings the engine up, so nothing reads the restart policies that would bring the containers back.

codes.meaning: This machine and the daemon speak different Docker API generations. Both ends settle on the older of the two, so everything works and anything newer than that generation is not available.
codes.name: API_MISMATCH
codes.remedy: Bring both to the same Docker release, or carry on with the older set. It is ordinary where the two machines were updated at different times.
codes.summary: Raised when this machine and the daemon speak different Docker API generations.

codes.meaning: No form was named, so there is nothing to start.
codes.name: NO_FORM_NAMED
codes.remedy: Name a form, or list the ones this stack has with `lemonfiber forms`.
codes.summary: Raised when no form was named.

codes.meaning: The stack declares no form by that name. Forms come from the stack rather than from lemonfiber, so a stack of your own may name them differently.
codes.name: NO_SUCH_FORM
codes.remedy: Use one of the names it offers. The message suggests the nearest match and lists the rest.
codes.summary: Raised when a named form is not declared by the stack.

codes.meaning: One of the forms you named has to run on its own — what it starts would conflict with the others rather than add to them.
codes.name: FORMS_CONFLICT
codes.remedy: Run that form by itself.
codes.summary: Raised when forms that cannot be combined are named together.

codes.meaning: Everything these forms would start needs a download provider, and none is configured. Starting them would give you services that cannot fetch anything.
codes.name: NOTHING_TO_RUN
codes.remedy: Add a Usenet provider, or a VPN and a torrent client, with `lemonfiber setup`.
codes.summary: Raised when narrowing leaves nothing to run.

codes.meaning: The request gate refused calls since the last check: something reaching the request service asked Sonarr, Radarr or Jellyfin for more than requests need, and the gate stopped it. The message lists the calls.
codes.name: REFUSED
codes.remedy: If nobody changed the request service's settings, check what it is running.
codes.summary: Raised when the request gate refused calls since the last diagnosis: the request service asked for something it has no use for.

codes.meaning: More entries reached the gate's record between two checks than it keeps, so some were dropped before they were read. What those entries were cannot be told now; the message says how many.
codes.name: LOST
codes.remedy: Run the diagnosis more often while this keeps happening.
codes.summary: Raised when more entries reached the gate's record between two diagnoses than it keeps, so some could not be reported.

codes.meaning: The removal that takes the library was confirmed without its own agreement. Destroying a library takes an answer given to that reading and no other.
codes.name: NEEDS_AGREEING
codes.remedy: Read what would go, then answer that reading by its own name, as in `lemonfiber uninstall media --agreed <name>`.
codes.summary: Raised when the tier that takes the library was confirmed without its own agreement.

codes.meaning: The agreement names a reading of this machine that is not the one standing now, so acting on it would act on something nobody saw.
codes.name: ANOTHER_READING
codes.remedy: Read it again, and answer the name it prints.
codes.summary: Raised when an agreement names a reading of this machine that is not the one standing now.

codes.meaning: The backup that comes before a destructive removal could not be taken, so nothing was removed. What these removals destroy cannot be made again, so it is taken behind a backup or not at all.
codes.name: NOT_BACKED_UP
codes.remedy: Deal with whatever stopped the backup — the message carries its reason — then ask for the removal again.
codes.summary: Raised when the backup a destructive removal takes first could not be taken.

codes.meaning: The hand-off is for nobody — the name was blank. The name is the account their device signs in to, so a blank one leads nowhere.
codes.name: NOBODY_NAMED
codes.remedy: Give the name they sign in as, as in `lemonfiber household handoff ana`.
codes.summary: Said where the hand-off is for nobody: the name is blank, or only spaces.

codes.meaning: This stack has no media server, so there is nothing for a device to sign in to. A hand-off points somebody's device at the media server and proves it signed in.
codes.name: NO_MEDIA_SERVER
codes.remedy: Add a media server to the stack and run setup.
codes.summary: Said where the stack holds no media server for a device to sign in to.

codes.meaning: The media server's own account has not been set up yet. Finding somebody's account and the devices signed in to it is done as the administrator, and this machine has not recorded one.
codes.name: NOT_SET_UP
codes.remedy: Run `lemonfiber setup`, so the media server's account is made and recorded.
codes.summary: Said where the media server's own account was never recorded.

codes.meaning: The account named administers the media server, so it is not one to hand over. This is the account lemonfiber signs in as, and a device handed it could change what everybody else in the household may watch.
codes.name: RUNS_THE_SERVER
codes.remedy: Invite the person under a name of their own, and hand that over.
codes.summary: Said where the account named administers the media server.

codes.meaning: This machine has no service manager lemonfiber can configure. The command can still be run, and it will still stop when the terminal running it closes.
codes.name: NOTHING_TO_HOST_WITH
codes.remedy: Keep the command running yourself, or arrange it with whatever this system uses to start things at login.
codes.summary: Raised where the platform has no service manager lemonfiber can configure.

codes.meaning: A service definition could not be written. Nothing was installed, so nothing is running and nothing was left behind.
codes.name: DEFINITION_UNWRITABLE
codes.remedy: Check that the directory exists and belongs to you, then try again.
codes.summary: Raised where a service definition could not be written.

codes.meaning: The service manager refused what it was asked. The definition that had been written was removed again, so nothing is half-installed.
codes.name: MANAGER_REFUSED
codes.remedy: Read what it said below, then try again once that is dealt with.
codes.summary: Raised where the service manager refused what it was asked.

codes.meaning: This machine will not say where lemonfiber keeps its own files.
codes.name: NOWHERE_TO_WRITE
codes.remedy: Set a home directory for this account, then install it again.
codes.summary: Raised when this machine will not say where it keeps its own files.

codes.meaning: This run cannot say where its own program is, so there is nothing to name in a service definition.
codes.name: NO_PROGRAM
codes.remedy: Run this again from an installed copy of lemonfiber rather than a piped one.
codes.summary: Raised when this run cannot say where its own program is.

codes.meaning: The guard is to be hosted against nothing — it was not told what to guard.
codes.name: NOTHING_NAMED_TO_GUARD
codes.remedy: Name the forms to guard, as you would when running the guard yourself.
codes.summary: Raised when the guard is to be hosted against nothing.

codes.meaning: This stack has no media server, so there is no account to offer. An invitation is an account somebody signs in to; without one there is nothing to invite them to.
codes.name: NO_MEDIA_SERVER
codes.remedy: Add a media server to the stack and run setup.
codes.summary: Said where the stack holds no media server: there is nothing to make an account on.

codes.meaning: The media server's own account has not been set up yet. Making somebody else an account is done as the administrator, and this machine has not recorded one.
codes.name: NO_CREDENTIAL
codes.remedy: Run `lemonfiber setup`, so the media server's account is made and recorded.
codes.summary: Said where the admin credential was never recorded: nothing can be asked of the server.

codes.meaning: This machine has no address the household could arrive at. An invitation is an address somebody else opens, and this machine answers to no name on the network and has none written down.
codes.name: NOWHERE_TO_SEND
codes.remedy: Record the address the household should use, with `lemonfiber config set HOUSEHOLD_HOST <address>`.
codes.summary: Said where this machine has no address the household could arrive at. An invitation is an address somebody else types. Sending one built from a default would be sending a link that opens nothing, which is worse than saying there is none: the operator would learn it had failed from whoever they invited.

codes.meaning: The invitation is for nobody — the name was blank. The name is what they will sign in as, so a blank one is an account nobody could use.
codes.name: NOBODY_NAMED
codes.remedy: Give the name they will sign in as, as in `lemonfiber invite ana`.
codes.summary: Said where the invitation is for nobody: the name is blank, or only spaces. The media server refuses this too, in its own words, which are `400` and a link to the specification of that status. The operator asked for something reasonable and mistyped it, and is owed a sentence about the name rather than about HTTP.

codes.meaning: An invitation offered again could not be dated again, so its window is not real. Their account is still there as it was; what could not be written down is when it was offered, which is what the window is counted from.
codes.name: WOULD_NOT_RENEW
codes.remedy: Check the configuration directory can be written, then run this again.
codes.summary: Said where an invitation offered again could not be dated again, so its window is not real. The account is untouched and still theirs — what failed is the write that says when it was offered. Reported rather than glossed over because the message the operator is about to send promises a window, and this one would be counted from whenever the invitation was first made, which has already passed.

codes.meaning: The media server would not say what libraries it holds, so nobody was invited. Choosing what somebody may open starts by finding the libraries, and that read did not answer.
codes.name: NO_LIBRARIES_READ
codes.remedy: Check the media server is running, then run this again.
codes.summary: Said where the media server would not say what libraries it holds. Refused rather than read as no libraries at all: a name matched against an empty list is a name that could not be found, and the operator would be told their library does not exist when what happened is that nobody could ask.

codes.meaning: No library goes by a name that was given, so nobody was invited. Libraries are named the way the media server's own screens name them, though not necessarily in the same capitalisation.
codes.name: NO_SUCH_LIBRARY
codes.remedy: Name a library the media server holds. The message lists the ones there are.
codes.summary: Said where no library goes by a name that was given. The ones there are, named: the fix is one word, and the words are already in hand.

codes.meaning: The media server would not set what the account may watch. A new account is taken back rather than left open to every library, so there is no invitation to send; an existing one is still there, allowed what it was allowed before.
codes.name: WOULD_NOT_ALLOW
codes.remedy: Run this again with the same choices, or set them in the media server's own settings.
codes.summary: Said where what the account may watch could not be written on it. A new account is taken back rather than left open, so the offer is refused whole; an existing one keeps what it already had. Said as which of the two is now true, because an operator told only that something failed would not know whether an open account is standing somewhere.

codes.meaning: When they were offered an account could not be written down, so it was not offered. An invitation runs out a set time after it is offered, and one this machine has no date for is taken back the next time anybody is invited.
codes.name: UNRECORDED
codes.remedy: Check the configuration directory can be written, then run this again.
codes.summary: Said where the offer could not be written down. An invitation runs out a set time after it is offered, and one this machine has no date for is taken back the next time anybody is invited — so an offer that could not be dated is not made.

codes.meaning: The media server would not ready the account to be claimed. An account is offered switched on, with a limit on wrong passwords, and the media server would not write either.
codes.name: UNGUARDED
codes.remedy: Check the media server is running, then run this again.
codes.summary: Said where the account could not be made one its person can claim: switched on, and bounded against guessing at its password.

codes.meaning: The name given is the account that administers the media server, so it is not one to offer. This is the account lemonfiber signs in as, and an invitation would put a household member's limits on it.
codes.name: RUNS_THE_SERVER
codes.remedy: Invite the person under a name of their own.
codes.summary: Said where the name given is the account that administers the media server. This is the account lemonfiber signs in as, and offering it would put a household member's limits on it.

codes.meaning: This run cannot say where lemonfiber keeps its own files. The configuration and data directories are worked out from this machine's own conventions, and that did not work here, so there is nothing to list and nothing safe to remove. Guessing at the usual place would risk naming a directory that is somebody else's.
codes.name: NOWHERE_KNOWN
codes.remedy: Run this as the account that installed lemonfiber, on a machine with a home directory it can read.
codes.summary: Raised when this run does not know where lemonfiber's own files go.

codes.meaning: That word cannot name a key. A key's name travels in an address, an alert and the journal, so it is lower-case letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, beginning with a letter or a digit, and at most 64 characters.
codes.name: BAD_NAME
codes.remedy: Name it as the program that holds it, as in `home-assistant`.
codes.summary: Raised when a key is asked for under a word that cannot name one.

codes.meaning: That is not a scope a key can have. A key has exactly one scope, and it decides everything the key admits.
codes.name: NOT_A_SCOPE
codes.remedy: Give it one of `read`, `act` or `member:<account>`.
codes.summary: Raised when a key is asked for with a scope that is none of the three.

codes.meaning: That is not a purpose a key can carry. A key says what it is for, so the listing can tell keys apart.
codes.name: NOT_A_PURPOSE
codes.remedy: Give it one of `home-assistant`, `mcp` or `other`.
codes.summary: Raised when a key is asked for with a purpose that is none of the three.

codes.meaning: The record of this machine's keys is there and does not read as keys. Nothing is written over it, because it may still hold keys somebody depends on, and every key it held is refused until it reads again. The message names the file.
codes.name: UNREADABLE
codes.remedy: Look at the file, and move it aside if it is damaged.
codes.summary: Raised when the record of keys is there and does not read as keys.

codes.meaning: A key by that name already exists, active or revoked. A name identifies one key for good, so an alert or a journal entry naming it always means the same key.
codes.name: NAME_TAKEN
codes.remedy: Mint it under another name.
codes.summary: Raised when a key is asked for under a name another key holds.

codes.meaning: Nobody in the household goes by that name. A member's key admits exactly what that member's own account does, so it is minted for an account the household holds.
codes.name: NO_SUCH_MEMBER
codes.remedy: Name them as they appear in the household, as `lemonfiber household` lists it.
codes.summary: Raised when a member's key names an account the household does not hold.

codes.meaning: The household could not be asked about that account, because the media server did not answer, so nothing was minted. A member's key is minted for an account the media server holds.
codes.name: UNASKED
codes.remedy: Try again once the media server is running.
codes.summary: Raised when the household could not be asked about a member's account.

codes.meaning: A household member mints and revokes only keys of their own. A member's key admits what their own account does and nothing more, so the only key a member may mint or revoke is one scoped to themselves.
codes.name: NOT_FOR_YOURSELF
codes.remedy: Ask for `member:<your own account>`, or ask whoever looks after this machine.
codes.summary: Raised when a household member asks for a key, or a revoke, that is not theirs alone.

codes.meaning: lemonfiber could not mint a secret for that key. A key's secret is unpredictable bytes this machine supplies, and it would not supply them, so nothing was minted.
codes.name: NO_SECRET
codes.remedy: Try again. If it happens twice, the operating system's own random source is at fault.
codes.summary: Raised when this machine would not supply the bytes a secret is made of.

codes.meaning: There is no active key by that name: none was minted under it, or it was revoked already, and the message says when.
codes.name: NO_SUCH_KEY
codes.remedy: List the keys with `lemonfiber key list`, and revoke one by the name it shows.
codes.summary: Raised when no active key holds the name a revoke gave.

codes.meaning: Whoever looks after this machine has not allowed household members to mint keys, so nothing was minted. A member's key carries that member's requests and viewing to whatever program holds it, so minting one is something the operator allows first.
codes.name: MEMBERS_MAY_NOT_MINT
codes.remedy: Ask whoever looks after this machine to allow it, with `lemonfiber config set LEMONFIBER_MEMBER_KEYS on`.
codes.summary: Raised when a household member asks to mint a key and the operator has not allowed members to.

codes.meaning: A service never reached a state that starting could accept, so the run did not finish starting.
codes.name: NEVER_SETTLED
codes.remedy: Look at what the service said, then start it again: `lemonfiber logs <service>`.
codes.summary: Raised when a service never reached a state that starting could accept.

codes.meaning: Stopping would take services out from under another form that is still running. Nothing was stopped.
codes.name: STILL_NEEDED
codes.remedy: Stop both if neither is wanted, or leave both up. A service two forms reach belongs to whichever you are using.
codes.summary: Raised when stopping would take a service out from under a form still running.

codes.meaning: Another lemonfiber run is already working on this stack, so this one stopped before doing anything. Two runs issuing commands about the same containers leave the stack in a state neither asked for.
codes.name: ALREADY_WORKING
codes.remedy: Wait for the other run to finish, then run this again. If you are sure that run is gone, `--force` takes the stack from it.
codes.summary: Another run is already working on this stack.

codes.meaning: Fetching images is switched off, so nothing was fetched. `LEMONFIBER_REACH_REGISTRY` is off, so this machine asks no registry for anything: a start uses the images already here, and a service whose image is missing will not start.
codes.name: REGISTRY_REFUSED
codes.remedy: Turn fetching back on with `lemonfiber config set LEMONFIBER_REACH_REGISTRY on`, then run this again.
codes.summary: Fetching images is switched off, so there was nothing to fetch with.

codes.meaning: The data location is not there, so nothing was started. Starting over a location that is not mounted does not fail — the engine makes the directory on whatever is underneath the mount point, usually the system disk, and the stack then files a second library into it while the real one is offline.
codes.name: NO_DATA_LOCATION
codes.remedy: Connect the drive or mount holding the data location, then start again. If it has moved for good, run setup and choose where it is now.
codes.summary: Raised when a start was asked for over a data location that is not there.

codes.meaning: A remote Docker context is in force, and the location the stack mounts is not on that machine. It is on this one, which is why the path looks right. Nothing was started, because Docker would have made an empty directory in its place and the services would have come up with nothing in them.
codes.name: ABSENT_THERE
codes.remedy: Make the location on that machine, or point lemonfiber at one that is there: `lemonfiber config set DATA_ROOT <path on that machine>`.
codes.summary: Raised when the stack's own location is not on the machine being operated.

codes.meaning: lemonfiber runs in a container, and a path the stack mounts is somewhere else on the machine underneath it, or not on that machine at all. Compose resolves every path the stack mounts on the machine, so the engine would mount whatever the machine keeps there, or make an empty directory in its place. Nothing was started; the message names both paths.
codes.name: ELSEWHERE_UNDERNEATH
codes.remedy: Mount the directory at the same path inside the container as on the machine, and point lemonfiber at that path.
codes.summary: Raised when a path the stack mounts is not at the same path on the machine under the container lemonfiber runs in.

codes.meaning: lemonfiber runs in a container and cannot reach Docker from inside it. It drives the stack through the host's Docker socket, which the templates mount at `/var/run/docker.sock`, and nothing answered there. Nothing was started.
codes.name: NO_ENGINE_IN_HERE
codes.remedy: Mount the host's Docker socket into the container at `/var/run/docker.sock`, as the templates do.
codes.summary: Raised when lemonfiber runs in a container that cannot reach the engine.

codes.meaning: The Docker lemonfiber reaches from its container is not the one running that container: the engine has no container by its name. Which paths on the machine stand behind the paths the container sees cannot be asked, so Compose would resolve them somewhere nobody checked. Nothing was started.
codes.name: NOT_ON_THIS_ENGINE
codes.remedy: Mount the socket of the engine running this container at `/var/run/docker.sock`.
codes.summary: Raised when the engine lemonfiber reaches from a container does not know that container.

codes.meaning: What was agreed to is not what a restart would restart now. A fresh look names other services — one added, removed or renamed since the restart was rehearsed — so nothing was restarted.
codes.name: RESTART_MOVED
codes.remedy: Rehearse the restart again, and answer the offer it gives now.
codes.summary: Raised where a restart names an offer that is not the one a fresh look at the stack builds.

codes.meaning: What you agreed to is not what standing in place of this setup would stop now. A fresh look offers something else — something started, stopped or changed since you read it — so nothing was stopped. The message names what replacing would stop now.
codes.name: OFFER_MOVED
codes.remedy: Ask what replacing would stop again, and read what it says now.
codes.summary: Raised when a replacement was agreed to for an offer that is not the one standing now.

codes.meaning: There is nowhere on this machine to keep what pairing a phone needs. The certificate a phone pins and the name it knows this stack by are kept beside the configuration, and this machine would not say where its configuration directory is.
codes.name: NOWHERE
codes.remedy: Run it as a user with a home directory, so there is a configuration directory.
codes.summary: Raised when there is nowhere to keep what pairing a phone needs.

codes.meaning: lemonfiber has not been served encrypted on your network, so a phone has nothing to reach. A phone refuses an address that presents no certificate, and reaches this machine from the network rather than from here. The material names the port the surface was last served on that way, and it has not been.
codes.name: NOT_SERVED
codes.remedy: Serve the web interface encrypted and on your network, on a port that stays the same: `lemonfiber ui --lan --tls --port <port>`.
codes.summary: Raised when the web surface has not been served encrypted on the network.

codes.meaning: The certificate this machine presents to a phone could not be read, or none has been made; the message says which. A phone pins that certificate, so it is not made again on its own — a new one is one every paired phone refuses.
codes.name: NO_CERTIFICATE
codes.remedy: Replace it with `lemonfiber companion certificate --confirm`, knowing every paired phone will need pairing again.
codes.summary: Raised when the certificate the surface presents cannot be read or made.

codes.meaning: This machine has no address a phone could reach it at. Pairing material names the address a phone reaches, and this machine answers to no name on the network and has none written down.
codes.name: NO_ADDRESS
codes.remedy: Record the address your household reaches this machine at, with `lemonfiber config set HOUSEHOLD_HOST <address>`.
codes.summary: Raised when this machine has no address a phone could reach it at.

codes.meaning: This stack's own identifier could not be read or made. A phone knows this stack by an identifier it keeps whatever else changes; the message says what went wrong.
codes.name: UNNAMED
codes.remedy: Check that the configuration directory can be written, and try again.
codes.summary: Raised when the stack's identifier cannot be read or made.

codes.meaning: That does not name anything the media server holds. A title is named by the identifier the shelf lists it under, which is thirty-two letters and digits.
codes.name: NOT_AN_ITEM
codes.remedy: Name a title by the `id` the shelf answered with.
codes.summary: Said where the title named is not something the media server could hold.

codes.meaning: That title is not on this member's shelf. Either the household does not hold it, or it is outside what this member may watch, and the two are answered alike.
codes.name: NOT_ON_THEIR_SHELF
codes.remedy: Choose a title from the shelf this member is shown.
codes.summary: Said where the title is not one this member may watch, or is not there at all.

codes.meaning: That does not name a device. A player names the device it plays on with an id it chose once and keeps: eight to sixty-four letters, digits and dashes.
codes.name: NOT_A_DEVICE
codes.remedy: Send the id the player keeps for this device.
codes.summary: Said where what names a member's device is not a device id.

codes.meaning: There is no media server to play from, or its own account was never recorded, so nothing can be asked of it for a member.
codes.name: NOTHING_TO_PLAY_FROM
codes.remedy: Add a media server to the stack and run `lemonfiber setup`.
codes.summary: Said where there is no media server to play from, or it was never set up.

codes.meaning: The media server did not answer, so nothing was read or recorded for this member. Nothing was changed.
codes.name: UNANSWERED
codes.remedy: Check the media server is running with `lemonfiber status`, then ask again.
codes.summary: Said where the media server would not answer for a member.

codes.meaning: Nobody was named. A grant and a player's progress are a member's own, so they are given for somebody in the household.
codes.name: NOBODY_NAMED
codes.remedy: Name the member, as the household lists them.
codes.summary: Said where nobody is named for something only a member can be.

codes.meaning: Nobody in this household is known by that, so there is nobody to grant or to record progress for.
codes.name: NOT_IN_THE_HOUSEHOLD
codes.remedy: Name somebody the household lists, by their name or their id.
codes.summary: Said where the member named is not somebody in the household.

codes.meaning: The media server has signing devices in by code turned off, so no session can be opened for the member's device without their password. Nothing was changed.
codes.name: SIGNS_NO_DEVICE_IN
codes.remedy: Turn Quick Connect on in the media server's dashboard, then grant again.
codes.summary: Said where the media server will not sign a device in by code.

codes.meaning: That title has no picture of that kind the media server serves as an image of at most two megabytes, so there is nothing to show.
codes.name: NO_SUCH_PICTURE
codes.remedy: Draw the title by its name where it has no picture.
codes.summary: Said where a title on the member's shelf has no picture of the kind asked for.

codes.meaning: A check a plugin contributed to the doctor did not hold. The meaning is the one the plugin declared with its first remedy; the message names the check, the plugin, and each fault found.
codes.name: CONTRIBUTED_FAILED
codes.remedy: Follow the remedies the plugin declared, in order. Where it declared none, the message says to ask the plugin's author.
codes.summary: A check a plugin contributed did not hold. One code for all of them rather than one per plugin, because a code is a stable thing an operator searches for and a plugin's own name is not this build's to mint one from. Which check and which plugin is on the finding, where it can be read.

codes.meaning: What was named is not a plugin lemonfiber can read. Nothing was installed or written.
codes.name: UNREADABLE
codes.remedy: Point at the plugin's directory, or at the `plugin.toml` inside it.
codes.summary: The source names no plugin this build can read.

codes.meaning: The plugin declares things lemonfiber will not install. The manifest is refused whole — nothing was written — and the message lists every violation at once.
codes.name: REFUSED
codes.remedy: Read what each one says, and take it up with whoever published the plugin.
codes.summary: The manifest is read and this build refuses what it declares.

codes.meaning: The record of what is installed could not be read, so lemonfiber will not say that nothing is installed. The message names the file.
codes.name: UNRECORDED
codes.remedy: Restore the file from a backup, or move it aside if nothing is installed.
codes.summary: The record of what is installed cannot be read.

codes.meaning: The plugin is already installed. Installing over it would be an update, and an install is not one. Nothing was changed; the message names the version installed.
codes.name: ALREADY
codes.remedy: Update it with `lemonfiber plugin update` on the new source, or remove it first.
codes.summary: The plugin is installed already.

codes.meaning: There is nowhere to install the plugin to: no stack directory has been set up.
codes.name: NOWHERE
codes.remedy: Run `lemonfiber setup` first, then install the plugin.
codes.summary: There is no stack on this machine to put a plugin's container in.

codes.meaning: A file the install needed could not be written. The install stopped where it was, and what it had written is on the change record.
codes.name: UNWRITABLE
codes.remedy: Check the permissions on the stack directory, then install it again. `lemonfiber history` shows what was written.
codes.summary: A directory or a document the install decided on would not land.

codes.meaning: The plugin held every proof and could not be recorded as installed, so the install was put back.
codes.name: UNRECORDABLE
codes.remedy: Check the permissions on the configuration directory, then install it again.
codes.summary: The wiring went down and the record of what is installed did not.

codes.meaning: The plugin's service would not start, so nothing about it could be proved, and the install was put back.
codes.name: UNPROVED
codes.remedy: Check that the stack is set up and the container engine is running, then install it again.
codes.summary: The plugin's own service would not start, so nothing about it could be proved.

codes.meaning: There is no installed plugin by that name, so nothing was removed. The message lists what is installed.
codes.name: NOTHING_TO_REMOVE
codes.remedy: See what is on this machine with `lemonfiber plugin installed`, and remove it by that id.
codes.summary: Nothing by that name is installed on this machine.

codes.meaning: The plugin is not installed, so there is nothing to update. Nothing was changed.
codes.name: NOTHING_TO_UPDATE
codes.remedy: Install it instead, with `lemonfiber plugin install` on the same source.
codes.summary: Nothing by that id is installed, so there is no version to replace.

codes.meaning: The installed version would not stop, so it was not updated. It is still installed, and nothing else changed.
codes.name: STUCK
codes.remedy: Check the container engine is running, then try the update again.
codes.summary: The version installed would not come off, so nothing else was touched.

codes.meaning: The plugin's service would answer on a hostname another plugin already answers on. The proxy will not start with two sites at one address, because that would bring down every route it serves.
codes.name: ANSWERED
codes.remedy: Give the plugin's service another hostname in its manifest, or remove the other plugin first.
codes.summary: Raised when a plugin's service would answer on a label another plugin's already does.

codes.meaning: The plugin is already installed from another source, and this is a second one for the same name. Two sources for one name are two plugins as far as anybody can tell, and which of them this machine runs is yours to choose. Nothing was written; the message names both sources.
codes.name: TWO_SOURCES
codes.remedy: To run the new source in its place, run `lemonfiber plugin update` on it. To keep the one installed, nothing needs doing.
codes.summary: Raised when a plugin is installed from a source other than the one its name is already installed from.

codes.meaning: Fetching a plugin from a git source is switched off on this machine, so the source was not asked. Nothing was fetched or installed.
codes.name: SOURCE_OFF
codes.remedy: Install it from a directory instead, or allow it with `lemonfiber config set LEMONFIBER_REACH_PLUGIN_SOURCE on`.
codes.summary: Raised when a plugin is named from a git source and fetching from one is switched off.

codes.meaning: The git source could not be fetched: it did not answer, or would not hand over the revision asked for. Nothing was installed, and the message carries what went wrong.
codes.name: UNFETCHED
codes.remedy: Check the address, and that this machine can reach it, then install it again.
codes.summary: Raised when a git source could not be reached or would not hand over a revision.

codes.meaning: The git source holds no branch, tag or commit by the name given. Nothing was fetched or installed.
codes.name: NO_REVISION
codes.remedy: Name a branch, a tag or a whole commit after the last `@`, or leave it off for what the source serves by default.
codes.summary: Raised when a git source holds no branch, tag or commit by the name given.

codes.meaning: The plugin was named for the catalogue to look up, and asking the catalogue is switched off on this machine. Nothing was fetched or installed.
codes.name: CATALOGUE_OFF
codes.remedy: Install it from a git source or a directory you name instead, or allow it with `lemonfiber config set LEMONFIBER_REACH_CATALOGUE on`.
codes.summary: Raised when a plugin is installed by name and asking the catalogue is switched off.

codes.meaning: The catalogue's index, or its signature, could not be fetched. Nothing was installed, and what is installed already is unaffected; installing from a git source or a directory does not ask the catalogue.
codes.name: CATALOGUE_UNREACHABLE
codes.remedy: Check this machine can reach github.com and install it again, or install it from its git source.
codes.summary: Raised when the catalogue's index or its signature could not be fetched.

codes.meaning: The catalogue's index is not signed by the key this build carries: it has no signature, one that does not verify, or none this build has a key to check. Nothing was resolved through it, because an index nobody can show the catalogue signed is no evidence that anybody reviewed anything.
codes.name: SIGNATURE_UNVERIFIED
codes.remedy: Install it from its git source, where it is installed as unreviewed, or install a lemonfiber that carries the catalogue's key.
codes.summary: Raised when the catalogue's index has no signature, one that does not verify, or none this build carries a key to check.

codes.meaning: The catalogue's index is signed and this build cannot read it. Nothing was resolved through it, and nothing was installed.
codes.name: CATALOGUE_UNREADABLE
codes.remedy: Update lemonfiber, whose newer releases read newer indexes, or install it from its git source.
codes.summary: Raised when the catalogue's index verified and is not one this build reads.

codes.meaning: The catalogue holds no plugin by that name. Nothing was fetched or installed.
codes.name: NOT_CATALOGUED
codes.remedy: Check the name, or write `./<name>` to install the directory of that name.
codes.summary: Raised when the catalogue holds no plugin by the name given.

codes.meaning: What the catalogue's origin holds at the commit it named is not what the catalogue reviewed: the manifest there is not the one whose digest it signed. Nothing was installed.
codes.name: NOT_AS_REVIEWED
codes.remedy: Install it from its git source if you mean to run it unreviewed, and tell the catalogue's maintainers.
codes.summary: Raised when what the catalogue's origin served is not what the catalogue reviewed.

codes.meaning: The plugin's service would be named as another installed plugin's service already is, once case and `-` or `_` are set aside. lemonfiber writes a plugin's container under its service's name and keeps what the service holds in settings named after it, so the two would be one container sharing one credential. Nothing was written; the message names both services.
codes.name: SPELLED_ALIKE
codes.remedy: Remove the other plugin first, or install a version of this one whose service is named otherwise.
codes.summary: Raised when a plugin's service would be named, where lemonfiber keeps what a service holds, as another installed plugin's service already is.

codes.meaning: That agreement was given for a different reading of the plugin: since it was read, the plugin, the stack or the record of what is installed changed. Agreeing to it now would be agreeing to something nobody saw, so nothing was changed; the message names what moved.
codes.name: PLUGIN_OFFER_MOVED
codes.remedy: Read it again, and answer the name it prints.
codes.summary: Raised when an install, an update or a removal answers an offer that was read against a plugin, a stack or a record that has since moved.

codes.meaning: A value a recipe would send to another host was not approved as itself, or an approval names a value and destination the reading does not list. Each value a recipe carries elsewhere is agreed to on its own, apart from the plugin, so nothing was changed.
codes.name: UNAPPROVED
codes.remedy: Approve each value the reading lists, by name, with `--approve`, and nothing else.
codes.summary: Raised when a value a recipe would carry to a destination was not approved as itself, or an approval names a pair the recipe does not carry.

codes.meaning: The source the update names holds a different plugin from the one it was asked to update. An update puts a new version of the installed plugin in its place, so nothing was changed.
codes.name: ANOTHER_PLUGIN
codes.remedy: Name a source that holds the plugin being updated, or install the other one on its own.
codes.summary: Raised when the source an update names holds a different plugin from the one it was asked to update.

codes.meaning: The plugin's service would take a name, a port or a label something on this machine already holds: a service of the stack or of your own overlay, another plugin's port, or a site the proxy already serves. Nothing was written; the message names each clash.
codes.name: OCCUPIED
codes.remedy: Rename or move what holds them, or install a version of the plugin that declares others.
codes.summary: Raised when a plugin's service would take a name, a port or a label something already on this machine holds: a service of the stack or of the operator's overlay, another plugin's port, or a site in the proxy's live configuration.

codes.meaning: The catalogue's index verifies and is older than one this machine has already verified. A release the catalogue has replaced is still signed, and what it reviewed may since have been withdrawn, so nothing was resolved through it and nothing was installed.
codes.name: CATALOGUE_REPLACED
codes.remedy: Try again later, when the catalogue serves its newest release, or install it from its git source.
codes.summary: Raised when the catalogue's index verifies and is older than the newest one this machine has verified.

codes.meaning: This machine cannot tell whether the catalogue's index is its newest: the record of the newest index it verified cannot be read or written. Without it, a release the catalogue has replaced would verify as though it were current, so nothing was resolved through it and nothing was installed.
codes.name: NEWEST_UNKEPT
codes.remedy: Check `catalogue.json` in the configuration directory, or install it from its git source.
codes.summary: Raised when the record of the newest catalogue index this machine verified cannot be read or written.

codes.meaning: The git source is named over a transport other than https, so nothing was asked of it and nothing was installed. A source fetched over anything else can be read or rewritten on its way here.
codes.name: SCHEME_REFUSED
codes.remedy: Name the same repository by its https address.
codes.summary: Raised when a git source is named over a transport other than https, before anything is asked of it.

codes.meaning: The git source's host is, or stands for, an address on this machine or on a network of its own — loopback, private, link-local or unspecified. A plugin is fetched only from somewhere every machine could reach, so nothing was fetched and nothing was installed.
codes.name: ADDRESS_REFUSED
codes.remedy: Install it from a directory on this machine, or from a public https address.
codes.summary: Raised when a git source's host is, or stands for, an address on this machine or on a network of its own: loopback, private, link-local or unspecified.

codes.meaning: The plugin's recipe substitutes a value into a header's name, which is a fixed identifier of the protocol and is written out. The manifest is refused whole — nothing was installed or written — and the message lists every other violation beside it.
codes.name: HEADER_NAMED
codes.remedy: Read what each one says, and take it up with whoever published the plugin.
codes.summary: Raised when a recipe substitutes a value into a header's name, which is a fixed identifier of the protocol and written out; the manifest's every other fault is listed beside it.

codes.meaning: A recipe of the plugin asks the operator for a value that was not given, or a value was given that no recipe of it asks for. Nothing was installed and nothing was written, and the message names each input.
codes.name: INPUT_UNMATCHED
codes.remedy: Give each input the plugin's recipes ask for, by name, and nothing else.
codes.summary: Raised when a recipe of the act asks the operator for a value that was not given, or a value was given that no recipe of the act asks for.

codes.meaning: A recipe's call names a host that is, or stands for, an address not out on the internet, so it was not sent. The install or update was put back, and the message names the steps that had run before it.
codes.name: CALL_REFUSED
codes.remedy: Read what the message says, and take it up with whoever published the plugin.
codes.summary: Raised when a recipe's call was not sent because its host stands for an address not out on the internet; the install or update was put back.

codes.meaning: A step of a recipe failed: nothing answered, the answer was not the one the recipe expects, a capture found nothing, or the answer was larger than any a recipe reads. The install or update was put back, and the message names the steps that had run before it.
codes.name: STEP_FAILED
codes.remedy: Check the service the recipe calls is running, then try again. If it keeps failing, take it up with whoever published the plugin.
codes.summary: Raised when a recipe's step failed any other way — nothing answered, the answer was not the one it expects, a capture found nothing, or the answer was larger than a recipe reads; the install or update was put back.

codes.meaning: A recipe's call path is not a plain absolute path. The manifest is refused whole — nothing was installed or written — and the message lists every other violation beside it.
codes.name: PATH_NOT_PLAIN
codes.remedy: Read what each one says, and take it up with whoever published the plugin.
codes.summary: Raised when a recipe's call path is not a plain absolute path; the manifest's every other fault is listed beside it.

codes.meaning: A recipe's call would have carried a value somewhere it may not go: not where the plugin's pairs say, not back to the service a credential belongs to, or outside without the operator's approval. It was not sent, and the install or update was put back.
codes.name: VALUE_WITHHELD
codes.remedy: Read what the message says, and take it up with whoever published the plugin.
codes.summary: Raised when a recipe's call was not sent because a value it carries may not go where it was going: not where its pairs say, not back to the service a credential belongs to, or outside without its approval; the install or update was put back.

codes.meaning: The program lemonfiber drives the engine through is not installed, so nothing can be started or stopped.
codes.name: MISSING_PROGRAM
codes.remedy: Install Docker Desktop, or Docker Engine on Linux.
codes.summary: Raised when the program a subprocess needs is missing.

codes.meaning: The program is installed and would not start. Usually a permission or daemon problem rather than a missing install.
codes.name: UNUSABLE_PROGRAM
codes.remedy: Check the container engine is running, then try again.
codes.summary: Raised when a program exists but will not start.

codes.meaning: A Usenet account has nothing left. It authenticates perfectly and can download nothing, which looks exactly like a broken stack from the outside. A block account does not refill on its own.
codes.name: PROVIDER_EMPTY
codes.remedy: Top the account up, or point the client at one that has data left.
codes.summary: Raised when an account has nothing left to serve.

codes.meaning: A Usenet account is running out, with time left to act. At the rate it is being used it runs out shortly, and downloads will stop with nothing else having changed.
codes.name: PROVIDER_LOW
codes.remedy: Top the account up before it runs out.
codes.summary: Raised when an account is running out, with time left to act.

codes.meaning: The subscription behind a Usenet account ends on the date recorded for it in the download client. When it lapses the account stops serving.
codes.name: PROVIDER_ENDING
codes.remedy: Renew the subscription, or clear its date in the client if it renews itself.
codes.summary: Raised when the subscription behind an account ends soon.

codes.meaning: An indexer has been failing and its aggregator has rested it. Searches through it are not coming back; the others still are, so releases are found from a smaller pool.
codes.name: INDEXER_RESTED
codes.remedy: Check the indexer's subscription and its status page, then test it in the aggregator.
codes.summary: Raised when an indexer has been failing and its aggregator has rested it.

codes.meaning: Every indexer is failing at once. Indexers do not all fail on the same afternoon, so the cause is almost always on this side of the connection.
codes.name: INDEXERS_ALL_FAILING
codes.remedy: Check this machine's network and DNS, and the tunnel if searches run through one.
codes.summary: Raised when every indexer is failing at once.

codes.meaning: A Usenet account is refusing the login. The provider answered the download client and rejected the credentials it offered. Every service stays green while nothing downloads.
codes.name: PROVIDER_REFUSED
codes.remedy: Check the account's username and password in the download client, and that the subscription behind it is still active.
codes.summary: Raised when an account refuses the credential the client offers it.

codes.meaning: A Usenet account has stopped answering the client entirely. That is the provider being down or the connection to it failing, rather than anything about the account — which is worth telling apart from a rejected login before changing anything.
codes.name: PROVIDER_SILENT
codes.remedy: Check the provider's status page and this machine's connection. The client picks the account up again on its own once it answers.
codes.summary: Raised when an account has stopped answering the client entirely.

codes.meaning: The download client is set to open more connections than the account allows, and the provider refuses the ones beyond the plan. Downloads still run on the rest, and the refusals read as an unreliable provider rather than as one setting too high.
codes.name: PROVIDER_CROWDED
codes.remedy: Lower the connection count for that account in the download client to what the plan includes.
codes.summary: Raised when the client is set to open more connections than an account allows.

codes.meaning: An indexer has spent the allowance recorded against it. Searches through it come back empty until it resets, and neither it nor the aggregator says so anywhere.
codes.name: INDEXER_CAPPED
codes.remedy: Wait for the allowance to reset, or raise the limit recorded for that indexer in the aggregator if the subscription allows more.
codes.summary: Raised when an indexer has spent the allowance recorded against it.

codes.meaning: The free space is thin for the chosen preset — it holds only a few hours of content at that quality. Nothing is broken and nothing already downloaded is affected; new acquisitions will simply fill the disk quickly.
codes.name: HEADROOM_LOW
codes.remedy: Free space, move the data location to a larger volume, or choose a lighter preset for the media that does not need it.
codes.summary: Raised when the free space holds too little content at the chosen quality.

codes.meaning: Releases exist for wanted content and the chosen preset wants none of them. The indexer is working; the preset is stricter than what can be found.
codes.name: PRESET_UNMET
codes.remedy: Choose a less demanding preset for that media, or wait for a matching release. The content stays wanted either way.
codes.summary: Raised when releases exist but the profile — the chosen quality included — wants none of them.

codes.meaning: A clean search turned up nothing at all for wanted content. The indexer answered — this is not an indexer failure — there is simply nothing to grab yet.
codes.name: NONE_AVAILABLE
codes.remedy: Check the indexer carries this content, or wait. No action is needed if it is merely not out yet.
codes.summary: Raised when a clean search turns up nothing at all for wanted content.

codes.meaning: The request service would not answer, so nothing was changed. What was in force before is still in force.
codes.name: UNREACHABLE
codes.remedy: Check the request service is running, then run this again.
codes.summary: Raised where the request service would not answer, so nothing was changed.

codes.meaning: A policy that lives inside a limit was chosen without one. Living within a limit needs a limit.
codes.name: NO_LIMIT
codes.remedy: Say how many requests a period allows, and how long the period is.
